_comment: Case-file check after the five-part hypothesis: spot the missing part in a new claim.

stem.en: A colleague drafts this claim for a study in one district: "Among men aged 40-60, smoking more than 10 bidis a day causes oral cancer in 5 per cent of them." Which of the five parts of a testable hypothesis is missing?

text.en: The population: the claim does not say which people it is about
The dose-response: the claim does not say how much smoking
The outcome: the claim does not name the disease expected
The time-response: the claim does not say how long until disease

explanation.en: The claim names the population (men aged 40-60), the cause (bidi smoking), the outcome (oral cancer) and a dose with a stated incidence (more than 10 a day, 5 per cent). It never says how many years of smoking come before the cancer, so a study could not tell an early effect from a late one.

hints.en: Go through the five parts one at a time and underline the words in the claim that state each one.
